content.text: The text reviews chronic biliary obstruction, describing liver shrinkage, enlarged gallbladder, jaundice, impaired digestion, pale or fatty stools, hemorrhagic tendency, renal injury, intermittent hepatic fever, cholaemia, neurological decline, and usually fatal progression. It discusses diagnosis and historical treatments for obstruction. Portal-vein thrombosis causes sudden ascites, splenomegaly, gastrointestinal bleeding, and abdominal-vein dilation; suppurative pylephlebitis causes septic fever and multiple hepatic abscesses. Liver hydatids are slow-growing elastic cysts diagnosed by imaging or aspirated fluid and treated mainly by puncture, aspiration, or surgery. Pancreatic diseases produce malnutrition, fatty stools, pain, jaundice, diabetes, cysts, pancreatitis, and cancer. The text also covers peritonitis, ascites, tuberculous or cancerous abdominal disease, and tabes mesenterica. In one case, a woman was moved from her country home to her city home before evaluation and repeated tapping.
